sources.title: Interview note preserving the multithreaded array-sort wording
Tagged question record for the multithreaded array-sort source
Independent exhaustive-small-domain and stress differential validation

claims.text: The recoverable source asks only for a multithreaded implementation of array sorting; it does not prescribe language, element type, ordering direction, stability, thread count or algorithm.
Java int[] ascending in-place sorting with caller-supplied parallelism/threshold and ForkJoin merge sort is an explicit answer-side executable contract.

The implementation matches independent standard-library sorting oracles across writer and reviewer suites; reviewer checks additionally cover exhaustive small arrays, larger deterministic stress shapes, integer extremes and declared argument rejection.

validation.command: extract candidate Java; javac -Xlint:all -Werror; exhaustive small-domain and deterministic stress differential checks versus Arrays.sort
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exhaustive_arrays=781 exhaustive_configs=4 stress_shapes=72 stress_configs=5 extremes=pass invalid=reject
checks: all 781 arrays of length 0..4 over {-2,-1,0,1,2} match Arrays.sort under four reviewer configurations
72 deterministic larger stress shapes match Arrays.sort under five reviewer configurations
declared null and non-positive parameter rejection

boundary_tests.expected: parallel siblings write disjoint half-open intervals and parent merge begins only after invokeAll completion
candidate does not claim multithreading is always faster and recommends measurement

findings: The primary source preserves only the request to implement array sorting with multiple threads; Java, int element type, ascending order, in-place mutation, parallelism, threshold and merge sort are not recovered source constraints.
The candidate explicitly labels those language/API/algorithm choices as an answer-side executable contract rather than attributing them to the interview source.

The concurrency argument is coherent: sibling tasks mutate disjoint half-open array intervals, invokeAll establishes child completion before the parent merge, and the shared temporary array is likewise written only within each task-owned interval while siblings run.

Reviewer-extracted Java compiles with warnings as errors and matches Arrays.sort for every array of length 0 through 4 over {-2,-1,0,1,2} under four independent parallelism/threshold configurations, plus 72 larger deterministic stress shapes under five configurations and integer-extreme cases.
Declared null and non-positive parallelism/threshold boundaries are enforced; complexity and serial-merge scalability limits are stated without claiming unmeasured production speedup.
No fabricated production experience, placeholder implementation, unsupported source expansion, or unresolved source variant was found.
